note:
PEOPLE THIS ARCHIVE ESTABLISHED FROM A DOCUMENT, NOT FROM THE SOURCE TREE.
The register is built from the MyHeritage harvest, which is somebody else's research. These seven are not in it and never were: they come out of Berlin civil registers and the 1939 census, read here. Adding them to the harvest file would have corrupted its provenance, so they are a THIRD CLASS with their own file, their own id block (9600000+) and their own label on the page.
EVERY ENTRY CARRIES ITS OWN BASIS. Some are a register entry read at the image; two are a text layer not yet confirmed at the image, and say so. NONE IS PROVED KIN TO DERRICK'S LINE, which is the same standing of the hundred people in the surname index.

people.name: Agnes Leibholz (Kerger)
people.basis: DOCUMENTED ALIVE, DEATH NOT FOUND. Born at MALLMITZ, KREIS SPROTTAU, SILESIA — today Małomice in Poland, so she had no home region left to return to after 1945. 1939 census supplementary card VZ153403, Bundesarchiv R 1509; "race" NNNN, four non-Jewish grandparents, so she is in a database of the persecuted only by marriage. Berlin directories and telephone books at Mehringdamm 109 from 1957 to 1979-80. NOT IN ANY WEST BERLIN DEATH REGISTER 1967-1994: all twelve boroughs read, year coverage verified, only Neukölln 1993-94 missing.

people.basis: DOCUMENTED. Standesamt Wilmersdorf, Sterberegister 1983 Nr. 304, read at the image. people.name: Hertha Leibholz
people.basis: *** NOT YET CONFIRMED AT THE IMAGE. *** Found in the TEXT LAYER of Standesamt Zehlendorf, Namensverzeichnis zum Sterberegister 1983, P Rep. 721 Nr. 2767 p.80: "Leibholz gesch. people.name: Gerda Felicitas Bade (Leibholz)
people.basis: DOCUMENTED, AND THE IMAGE CANNOT CONFIRM IT — WHICH REVERSES THIS ARCHIVE'S USUAL RULE. Standesamt Wilmersdorf, Sterberegister 1993 Nr. 312, P Rep. 570 Nr. 3306. Both her entries were opened on 9 October: “Bade geb. Leibholz, Gerda Felicitas, 15.02.1993” on page 7 under B and “Leibholz, Gerda Felicitas, 15.02.1993” on page 74 under L, THE SAME NUMBER 312 FROM TWO UNRELATED POSITIONS SIXTY-SEVEN PAGES APART — the series checking itself. The page SCAN is a faint degraded photocopy and her line is barely resolvable, so there is no image confirmation; for these 1993 volumes the text layer is NOT OCR of that scan but a clean born-digital transcription, and it is the better witness. SHE WAS BORN A LEIBHOLZ AND MARRIED OUT, so she had Leibholz parents in Berlin within living memory and is the only one of the seven pointing upward. HER FATHER IS NOT REACHABLE FREE: the marriage indexes stop at 1944 and every volume tested is completely blind, and her index entry carries no birth date to narrow by. Sterberegister Wilmersdorf 1993 Nr. 312 would name her parents outright.

facts.c: Sterberegister Wilmersdorf 1993 Nr. 312 — text layer only, not confirmed at the image

people.name: Johanne Klara Leipsholz (Diedring)
people.basis: DOCUMENTED, READ AT THE IMAGE. Standesamt Kreuzberg, Sterberegister 1960 Nr. 316, P Rep. 510 Nr. 679 p.123 under the Februar heading; religion column a dash. THE SURNAME IS SPELT LEIPSHOLZ, WITH AN S — a ninth spelling of this name and a registrar's own, not a machine's, read at five times magnification. STRONG CANDIDATE, NOT PROVED, for the KLARA LEIPHOLZ, Putzmacherin, of SW 29 Dieffenbachstraße 58 who is in the Berlin directories of 1957 and 1959 and gone after: the forename is Klara, the borough is Kreuzberg, and she died in the FIRST BLIND YEAR after her last directory entry, with 1959 read at the image and empty and 1963-1994 swept and empty. Against it: the spelling differs by a letter and “geb. Diedring” is a maiden name this archive has never held. Kreuzberg 1960 Nr. 316 gives the last address and settles it. NOT KIN TO ANYONE HERE ON ANY EVIDENCE.

facts.c: Sterberegister Kreuzberg 1960 Nr. 316, "Leipsholz geb. Diedring", no confession stated

people.name: Georg Rosenberg
people.basis: DOCUMENTED. Yad Vashem, Central Database of Shoah Victims' Names, Page of Testimony item 1057746: born Schlochau 3 December 1888, a Kaufmann, of Berlin before and during the war, murdered aged 54, place of death Auschwitz, with no date. A second Page (item 423812) gives the same birth to the day, the same town and the same trade. His sister Jenny married a Leipholz of Berlin. NOT PROVED KIN to the Schubin Leibholz family or to any Luwinski: Rosenberg is among the commonest Jewish surnames in Germany. Found by searching the database's submitter tab, 11 October 2026.

facts.c: Yad Vashem Page of Testimony item 1057746; a second Page, item 423812, agrees to the day
Kaufmann, Page of Testimony 1057746
Murdered, aged 54, place of death Auschwitz, no date given (Page of Testimony 1057746)

people.name: Joseph Ehrlich
people.basis: DOCUMENTED, in four places. The Bundesarchiv memorial list, the Berlin deportation list and the Theresienstadt inmate list agree: born at Reetz in Pomerania, of Berlin, deported from Berlin to Theresienstadt on 17 March 1943, dead there on 1 February 1944. A Yad Vashem Page of Testimony (item 5369883) disagrees on two fields, giving 7 November 1862 and 1943; the lists win on both, as the page of testimony is written from memory, often decades later. NOT PROVED KIN to the Schubin Leibholz family: he is the father-in-law of a Georg Rosenberg and belongs to a second family entirely.

facts.c: Bundesarchiv memorial list and Berlin deportation list; the Page of Testimony says 7 November
Berlin deportation list; Theresienstadt inmate list
Theresienstadt inmate list and Bundesarchiv memorial list; the Page of Testimony says 1943 and loses

people.name: Joachim Peter Leibholz
people.basis: DOCUMENTED. Born at Berlin on 20 August 1903 and registered at Standesamt Charlottenburg I (birth found 11 October 2026). Landed at Melbourne from the Anchises on 12 June 1939 (National Archives of Australia, passenger statement A12508, 21/2464); naturalised at South Yarra in 1944 (A714, 18/8913); died at Toorak in 1971, aged 68, registration 26252/1971 in the Victorian death index, which names his parents as William Leibholz and Nanette née Netter. NOT PROVED KIN to the Schubin Leibholz family: nothing joins them but the surname. Known in Melbourne as Peter.

facts.c: Landesarchiv Berlin, Charlottenburg I birth index; NAA A12508, 21/2464
NAA A12508, 21/2464: arrived per Anchises
NAA A714, 18/8913, naturalisation index card

people.name: Gertrud Eisenberg (Haake)
people.basis: DOCUMENTED, DEATH NOT FOUND. Born 9 June 1879 (1939 census database of persecuted people, where she is entered as Trude Eisenberg née Haake): a commercial court councillor's widow who owned the building at Treuchtlinger Straße 4, Berlin, and lived in it on census night, 17 May 1939. The Berlin directory of 1941 enters the house under the owner, "Eisenberg, G. Sara, Ww.", carrying the compulsory Sara. NOT PROVED KIN. Born 1879, so not living by the estate's rule on the date alone.

people.name: Elisabeth Weiler (Leipholz)
people.basis: DOCUMENTED, SURVIVED, DEATH NOT FOUND. The Bundesarchiv Residents' List (ID 1166673) enters Elisabeth Weiler née Leipholz, born 1 January 1891 at Neustettin in Pomerania, of Berlin, persecuted on racial grounds, emigrated to Palestine; she is not in the Gedenkbuch because she survived. Mapping the Lives gives Berlin as the birthplace. A first of January is the commonest placeholder for a year known without a day, so only the year is taken. NOT PROVED KIN: the first person the eighth spelling of the surname produced. Born 1891, so not living by the estate's rule on the date alone.
